root_cause.text: MPTCP initialized `tcpv6_prot_override` too early by copying `tcpv6_prot` before `proto_register(&tcpv6_prot)` had set up its RCU-safe slab cache, leaving `tcpv6_prot_override.slab` NULL and causing IPv6 subflow child sockets to be allocated from non-`SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU` `kmalloc` memory used by lockless `__inet_lookup_established`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states `mptcp_subflow_init()` ran during `inet_init()` before `inet6_init()` called `proto_register(&tcpv6_prot)`, so "`tcpv6_prot.slab` is still NULL, so `tcpv6_prot_override.slab` remains NULL permanently," and the fix moves IPv6 setup into `mptcp_subflow_v6_init()` called from `mptcp_proto_v6_init()` to ensure the override inherits the `SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU` slab.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize IPv6 MPTCP subflow support during mptcp_proto_v6_init() so required IPv6 subflow setup is not missed.
intent_record.what: A call to mptcp_subflow_v6_init() was added at the start of mptcp_proto_v6_init(), before initializing mptcp_v6_prot fields.
intent_record.how: At runtime, IPv6 MPTCP protocol initialization now explicitly initializes the IPv6 MPTCP subflow support before setting up the IPv6 protocol structure, ensuring required IPv6 subflow setup occurs during module init instead of being skipped.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the missing IPv6 subflow initialization prototype so it can be invoked when MPTCP IPv6 support is enabled.
intent_record.what: A new function declaration, "void __init mptcp_subflow_v6_init(void);", was added inside the CONFIG_MPTCP_IPV6 conditional block alongside the existing IPv6 MPTCP init prototype.
intent_record.how: This makes the IPv6 subflow initialization function visible to other compilation units when IPv6 MPTCP support is enabled, allowing it to be called during initialization instead of remaining undeclared.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register and initialize the MPTCP subflow ULP during startup, failing hard on registration errors, while splitting IPv6-specific setup into a separate init function.
intent_record.what: The diff adds a call to mptcp_diag_subflow_init(&subflow_ulp_ops), then adds a tcp_register_ulp(&subflow_ulp_ops) registration call with a panic on failure inside mptcp_subflow_init(), closes that function earlier, and introduces a new __init function named mptcp_subflow_v6_init() under the CONFIG_MPTCP_IPV6 conditional to hold the subsequent IPv6-specific initialization code.
intent_record.how: At runtime, MPTCP subflow ULP operations are now explicitly initialized for diagnostics and registered with the TCP ULP framework during subflow initialization, causing the kernel to abort boot/init if registration fails instead of proceeding without subflow ULP support. The IPv6-specific initialization logic is separated into its own init function, allowing distinct setup sequencing for generic subflow registration versus IPv6-only initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move the MPTCP subflow diagnostic initialization and ULP registration out of this conditional/location by adjusting the #endif scope.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the call to mptcp_diag_subflow_init(&subflow_ulp_ops) and the subsequent tcp_register_ulp(&subflow_ulp_ops) registration-and-panic block from the shown location inside mptcp_subflow_init(), and moves a closing #endif so that the function now ends before that preprocessor directive.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this shown code no longer performs subflow diagnostic initialization or registers the subflow ULP from this location in mptcp_subflow_init(). The adjusted preprocessor boundary changes the conditional compilation scope, indicating that this initialization/registration logic is being excluded from this code path or handled elsewhere.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure IPv6 MPTCP subflow support is properly initialized by declaring and invoking the missing IPv6 subflow initialization during MPTCP IPv6 setup.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is caused by incorrect IPv6 MPTCP subflow/protocol initialization ordering. This group adds the missing IPv6 subflow initialization during MPTCP IPv6 setup, which directly affects whether the IPv6 subflow protocol state is properly initialized and is therefore tied to the root cause rather than being unrelated refactoring.

The change directly affects MPTCP subflow startup/initialization order and moves IPv6-specific setup into a separate init path, which is closely tied to the root cause of initializing the IPv6 protocol override too early before tcpv6_prot was fully registered.

The change only moves subflow diagnostic initialization and ULP registration by adjusting preprocessor/conditional scope. It does not address the early copy/initialization ordering of tcpv6_prot_override, proto_register(&tcpv6_prot), or the NULL slab/RCU-safe allocation issue at the root of the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This conditional marks the pre-fix IPv6 subflow setup path that was executed too early during startup. The root cause was that IPv6 override initialization happened before tcpv6_prot had been fully registered, so this is the closest visible pre-fix location tied to the premature IPv6-specific initialization.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix IPv6 initialization path is the only exact statement provided from the vulnerable code region. It gates the premature IPv6-specific subflow setup that initialized the MPTCP IPv6 protocol override before tcpv6_prot had been fully registered and its RCU-safe slab set up, leading to a NULL slab in the override.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the initialization of the MPTCP IPv6 protocol-related overrides in this commit and whether they are copied before the underlying TCPv6 proto is registered/finalized. The root cause is early initialization of an IPv6 proto override by copying tcpv6_prot before proto_register(&tcpv6_prot) has set the RCU-safe slab cache, leaving the copied .slab NULL. In this commit, IPv6-specific MPTCP support is introduced and initialized in mptcp_subflow_init() via direct structure copies such as "subflow_v6_specific = ipv6_specific;" and setup of IPv6 handlers. There is no logic here that delays IPv6 override/proto copying until after tcpv6_prot registration, nor any explicit repair of an inherited slab pointer for an IPv6 proto override. The code shows the vulnerable pattern is being introduced for IPv6 support without the later fix. In particular, the function adds CONFIG_MPTCP_IPV6 handling and initializes IPv6-specific ops early in module init, but there is no code ensuring a registered/properly initialized tcpv6-based proto object with a valid SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU slab. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present in this commit version, and the fix is absent.
